title: Certificates of Deposit: Topping Up in Grace to Reach the Jumbo Bonus on Renewal
content:
While a certificate from Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit sits in its grace period, an owner may ask for a deposit sized so that the renewed term clears the Jumbo Bonus threshold, and by no more than that. This page covers that top-up and the customer's tool for making it.

## The top-up

The sum is set by how far the certificate falls short of the Jumbo Bonus threshold. The money comes from the owner's own active PCB savings or money market account and is added as a grace add-on. Making the transfer is the owner's own act; if no top-up can be accepted, nothing is added.

## The customer's tool: `add_grace_deposit_522b16cc`

### Owner of the action

The tool is the customer's, not the agent's. The agent's part is to unlock it for the customer by means of `unlock_user_discoverable_tool`, which passes it across; the customer themselves executes it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

### Business effect

A run posts one grace add-on deposit entry on a matured certificate during its grace period, dated the current day, recording where the money came from and a freshly assigned 15-digit posting trace number. The certificate's principal balance rises by the deposited sum at once. The certificate remains in its grace period.

### Inputs

| Input | Content | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | reference number of the certificate's owner, taken by the agent from the customer profile lookup and given to the customer | customer reference number |
| `certificate_id` | reference number of the certificate receiving the money, taken by the agent from the certificate lookup and given to the customer | certificate reference number |
| `amount` | the sum paid in | USD, 2 decimal places, positive |
| `funding_source` | the origin of the money | one of `none` (not for deposits), `pcb_checking` (moved in-house out of the owner's PCB checking), `pcb_savings` (moved in-house out of the owner's PCB savings or money market holding), `external_ach` (ACH from another bank), `check` (a check paid into the certificate), `cash` (cash at a branch), `wire` (incoming wire) |
| `counterparty_account_id` | the owner's PCB checking or savings account the money leaves, for an internal transfer, as the account lookup returns it | account reference number; an empty string for any other source |

### Receipt

When it succeeds, the tool returns `deposit_id` (the reference of the grace add-on deposit entry), `certificate_id`, `amount` (USD to 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD), `trace_number` (15 digits) and `principal_balance` (principal after the deposit, to the cent). A `deposit_id` in the receipt means the grace add-on has posted.

## Basis Q&A

**Does the tool decide how much may be added?** No. It posts whatever sum is entered; the size of a proper top-up comes from the certificate's grace top-up terms.
